arxiv-2010-15587.title: Important Influence of Entrance Channel Reorientation Coupling on Proton Stripping
arxiv-2010-15587.creator: N. Keeley, K. W. Kemper, K. Rusek
arxiv-2010-15587.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by N. Keeley, K. W. Kemper, K. Rusek. While it is well established that the ground state reorientation coupling can have a significant influence on the elastic scattering of deformed nuclei, the effect of such couplings on transfer channels has been much less well investigated.

arxiv-2205-00174.title: Single-photon scattering on a qubit. Space-time structure of the scattered field
arxiv-2205-00174.creator: Ya. S. Greenberg, A. G. Moiseev, A. A. Shtygashev
arxiv-2205-00174.description: Abstract We study the space-time structure of the scattered field induced by the scattering of a narrow single-photon Gaussian pulse on a qubit embedded in 1D open waveguide. For a weak excitation power we obtain explicit analytical expressions for space and time dependence of reflected and transmitted fields which are, in general, are different from plain travelling waves.

arxiv-2303-05888.title: A Distributionally Robust Random Utility Model
arxiv-2303-05888.creator: Emerson Melo, David Müller, Ruben Schlotter
arxiv-2303-05888.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Emerson Melo, David Müller, Ruben Schlotter. This paper introduces the distributionally robust random utility model (DRO-RUM), which allows the preference shock (unobserved heterogeneity) distribution to be misspecified or unknown. We make three contributions using tools from the literature on robust optimization. First, by exploiting the notion of distributionally robust social surplus function, we show that the DRO-RUM endogenously generates a shock distribution that incorporates a correlation between the utilities of the different alternatives.

arxiv-2308-00466.title: Could electromagnetism be envisaged as a form of gravity in a metric affine framework?
arxiv-2308-00466.creator: Panagiotis Mavrogiannis
arxiv-2308-00466.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Panagiotis Mavrogiannis. We revisit the relativistic coupling between gravity and electromagnetism, putting particularly into question the status of the latter; whether it behaves as a source or as a form of gravity on large scales. Considering a metric-affine framework and a simple action principle, we find out that a component of gravity, the so-called homothetic curvature field, satisfies both sets of Maxwell equations. Therefore, we arrive at a gravito-electromagnetic equivalence analogous to the mass-energy equivalence.

arxiv-2405-08781.title: Total coloring of regular graphs of girth = degree + 1
arxiv-2405-08781.description: Abstract Let 2 ≤ k ∈ ℤ 2\leq k\in\mathbb{Z} . A total coloring of a k k -regular simple graph via k + 1 k+1 colors is an efficient total coloring if each color yields an efficient dominating set, where the efficient domination condition applies to the restriction of each color class to the vertex set.

arxiv-2409-08082.title: Quantum Information Resources in Spin-1 Heisenberg Dimer Systems
arxiv-2409-08082.creator: Fadwa Benabdallah, M. Y. Abd-Rabbou, Mohammed Daoud, Saeed Haddadi
arxiv-2409-08082.description: Abstract We explore the quantum information resources within bipartite pure and mixed states of the quantum spin-1 Heisenberg dimer system, considering some interesting factors such as the l 1 l_{1} -norm of quantum coherence, relative coherence, negativity, and steering, influenced by the magnetic field and uniaxial single-ion anisotropy.

arxiv-2502-06514.title: Fractional interacting particle system: drift parameter estimation via Malliavin calculus
arxiv-2502-06514.creator: Chiara Amorino, Ivan Nourdin, Radomyra Shevchenko
arxiv-2502-06514.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chiara Amorino, Ivan Nourdin, Radomyra Shevchenko. We address the problem of estimating the drift parameter in a system of N N interacting particles driven by additive fractional Brownian motion of Hurst index H ≥ 1 / 2 H\geq 1/2 . Considering continuous observation of the interacting particles over a fixed interval [ 0 , T ] [0,T] , we examine the asymptotic regime as N → ∞ N\to\infty .

uslaw-usc-t42-s1437m.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 8 (Low-Income Housing); Subchapter I (General Program Of Assisted Housing). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Any of the following may be used as the non-Federal share required in connection with activities undertaken under Federal grant-in-aid programs which provide social, educational, employment, and other services to the tenants in a project assisted.

uslaw-usc-t7-s1930.title: 7 U.S.C. § 1930 — Continued availability of appropriated funds for direct real estate loans to farmers and ranchers
uslaw-usc-t7-s1930.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t7-s1930.description: United States Code, Title 7 (Agriculture); Chapter 50 (Agricultural Credit); Subchapter I (Real Estate Loans). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Funds appropriated for the purpose of making direct real estate loans to farmers and ranchers under this subchapter shall remain available until expended.
